tasks.title: The gates and test:affected run in the php-baseimages dev image, locally as in CI
tasks.goal: Sylvester decided 30 September: the cboxdk php-baseimages dev image (ghcr.io/cboxdk/php-baseimages/php-cli:8.5-bookworm-dev-v1: PHP 8.5, PCOV, Xdebug, SPX, Node 22 and Playwright's Chromium in /ms-playwright) is used everywhere, locally as in CI, as dogfooding. CI already runs in it (ci.yml, compose.ci.yaml, docker/ci-setup.sh). Make the local runs use it too, for the current checkout, a linked worktree included: (1) composer check runs its steps in the image, with the same gates, steps, suites and flags as today, so nothing is skipped or weakened (GUARDRAILS 7.3); (2) composer test:affected runs vendor/bin/pest --parallel --tia with any extra arguments in the image, for fast feedback while working (Pest 5 test impact analysis records per test the files and tables it touches through PCOV and reruns only the affected tests); it is not a gate; (3) the Browser suite (gate 8) can run locally in the image with its Chromium. Mount the checkout at the same absolute path as on the host and use it as the working directory (the testkit derives the checkout's own test database from that path, so two worktrees never share one); run as the host user's uid and gid (file permission tests skip as root); join the network of the shared services of the main checkout's compose.yaml and reach Postgres and Valkey by their service names; mount the host's ~/.pest so the TIA graph is shared; never start or recreate the shared services, and fail with the fix when they are down. Solve what differs between the host and the Linux image rather than excluding it: node_modules with platform binaries installed on macOS (for example a separate Linux node_modules volume per checkout, or npm ci in the image), and the file system speed of bind mounts on macOS (measure composer check wall time on the host and in the image and record both in PROGRESS.md). Update CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and the developer docs, which today say the host runs the gates and the php container mounts only the main checkout. An interrupted earlier attempt left commits named wip4 and wip5 on branch wip/M1-T68 (worktree ~/Projects/Cbox/cms-worktrees/M1-T68, HEAD ca47233): reuse what is right and leave the branch with commits named "M1-T68: <what>".
acceptance: composer check from a linked worktree runs every gate step inside the dev image with the same steps, suites and flags as before (show the report), using that worktree's own test database, and passes
composer test:affected from a linked worktree records the TIA graph once and then, after one source file changes, runs only the dependent tests and replays the rest (show the counts)
vendor/bin/pest --testsuite=Browser runs locally in the image with its Chromium and passes
Runs are as the host user, not root, and fail with a clear message when the shared services are down; a test covers the docker command built (mounts, user, network, environment) with a fake docker
composer check:selftest passes with every planted violation caught; the containerized CI run passes
composer check wall time on the host and in the image is recorded in PROGRESS.md

tasks.title: Surface contract tests generated from the actions registry
tasks.goal: MILESTONES M1 point 6 and GUARDRAILS 2.1 and 9 ('én per action og overflade'). A Pest dataset built from the compiled actions registry yields one contract test per action and surface (REST, Inertia, MCP, CLI) for all eight M1 commands. Each test checks a field error, a version conflict, dry-run, and a receipt that is committed but has not reached its wait level. A new action gets its surface tests without writing them by hand, and a surface without a profile fails the suite. An interrupted earlier attempt left uncommitted changes in worktree ~/Projects/Cbox/cms-worktrees/M1-T42 on branch wip/M1-T42: reuse what is right.

tasks.title: A third fixture type, added only as a schema file, end to end
tasks.goal: The M1 exit criterion that proves GUARDRAILS 2.4. Add a third fixture type to workbench/schema, with handles prefixed fixture_. Its fields and capabilities differ from both others: history audit-only, stages draft-release, routable, and field types the other two do not use. Run cms:generate and commit the generated code and migration. Change nothing in the source modules: this task's commit touches only workbench/ and tests/. Add tests/Postgres/WalkingSkeleton/ThirdTypeTest.php. It creates, revises, releases and publishes an entry of the type, places it, resolves it over GET /v1/resolve, checks its fragment invalidation, and runs the generated surface contract tests for its commands. It also shows that a rebuild from head snapshots gives identical rows.
acceptance: vendor/bin/pest --testsuite=Postgres tests/Postgres/WalkingSkeleton/ThirdTypeTest.php passes
git show --stat of this task's commit lists no file under packages/, only workbench/ and tests/

tasks.title: main green on GitHub CI within the 15-minute budget
tasks.goal: GitHub CI (ci.yml, bin/ci, the PR profile) has not passed on main since 1487b6e (29 September): runs fail or are cancelled by the job timeout of 20 minutes. Known causes: mutation on changed files ran no mutations because Tests\Arch\MarkersTest threw a RuntimeException inside the mutation run (run on cfbb6f5); ConnectionQueryTransactionBehaviourTest fails in the Postgres suite of the containerized run with read_audit_actor_id_fkey (found by M1-T45 and the T47+T48 integration); mutation scores below 80 for the seeding classes of M1-T47 (SeedRequestLimits, SeedText and others); and the wall time exceeds the 15-minute budget of GUARDRAILS 10. Fix every cause at its root: tests that kill the surviving mutations, fixes of the failing tests or the code, and parallelism (GUARDRAILS 10: parallelize, never cut). Never lower the mutation threshold, exclude classes, skip tests or raise the job timeout above what the budget allows (GUARDRAILS 7.3). Work on the main of this run after T65, T38, T42, T50, T58 and T59 are merged, so the fix covers the whole block.
acceptance: docker compose -f compose.ci.yaml run --rm ci exits 0 on HEAD with CMS_CI_BASE_REF set to the commit before the block (59f0d88), and its bin/ci wall time is recorded under 15 minutes
The mutation steps print a report and every changed class scores at least 80

blockers: M0-T47 (open under 'Til review af Sylvester'): whether the testkit's shared contract suites are left out of mutation on changed files. They live in src and get mutated, although no test can catch a mutated assertion. M1 adds several new shared suites (identity, type catalog, fragment store, CDN driver, telemetry), so E11 may fail only on them. The plan keeps them in scope as today. If E11 fails only on shared-suite assertions, the main session records it for Sylvester and does not weaken the gate.

Outward-facing names that M1 introduces beyond what the PRD fixes. These are error codes beyond the PRD's (T10), REST paths other than /v1/resolve (T38), CLI command names and the configuration key for the CLI's service credential (T39), MCP tool names (T41), the addon manifest's file name and keys (T44), the fixture addon's namespace (T45), and the exact holder line in LICENSE (T7; MIT itself is fixed by the PRD). The tasks name them after the PRD's wording and list them under 'Til review af Sylvester'. This does not block M1.

Gate 11 (review by someone other than the author) needs branch protection with required reviews on main in github.com/cboxdk/cms. That is a repository setting for Sylvester. T2 only corrects the reason; the gate stays reported as not run.

Possible: cboxdk/laravel-operations may not install on PHP 8.5 and Laravel 13. T57 checks it without changing the package. If it fails, the need goes under 'Til review af Sylvester' (GUARDRAILS 3), and T46 and T47 run their chunk actions from a console command under a recorded interpretation, so E5 and E7 do not depend on it.

Not blocking, for awareness: in M1, service credentials, actors, grants, roles, sites, nodes and routes are created only by testkit fixtures, because token issuance, login, grant commands and node commands are B1 and B2 by the build order. Real CDN drivers are B4, replica routing by consistency token is B4 and B5, planned transitions are B3, and upcasters are B3. The tasks record these as interpretations, not as decisions for Sylvester.
